t: Section 545(2) of title 11, United States Code, is amended by inserting before the semicolon at the end the following: “, except in any case  in which a purchaser is a purchaser described in section 6323 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or in any other similar provision of State or local law”.

fable.w: This section only amends the Bankruptcy Code's statutory-lien avoidance provision to add an exception for purchasers described in section 6323 of the Internal Revenue Code or similar State or local law. The tempting reading is that the reference to "State or local law" brings in outside parties, but it is a cross-reference to substantive law, not consultation or coordination with states or localities. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: or in any other similar provision of State or local law

opus.w: This is a technical amendment to the Bankruptcy Code's rule on avoiding statutory liens. It adds an exception for certain protected purchasers. The reference to 'State or local law' only points to similar legal provisions; it doesn't ask states, localities, or anyone else to take part in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to challenge a federal decision.
opus.s: except in any case  in which a purchaser is a purchaser described in section 6323 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or in any other similar provision of State or local law
opus.b:
1. **Analysis.** This section amends the Bankruptcy Code's rule on when a trustee can avoid statutory liens. It adds an exception for certain purchasers. The tempting reading is that mentioning "State or local law" brings outside parties in. It doesn't: the phrase only points to similar state or local legal provisions. No one outside the federal government is consulted, coordinated with, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue over a federal decision. No rulemaking is authorized either.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a definition in the Bankruptcy Code to exclude certain purchasers based on existing state or local laws. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from state or local governments, the public, or any other outside party before making a decision. The reference to state law is substantive, not procedural.
qwen_chat.s: Section 545(2) of title 11, United States Code, is amended by inserting before the semicolon at the end the following: “, except in any case  in which a purchaser is a purchaser described in section 6323 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or in any other similar provision of State or local law”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that referencing "State or local law" implies some form of coordination or consultation with state or local governments. However, the text merely defines an exception to a federal rule based on existing state laws; it does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from state or local officials before making a decision. It is a substantive legal definition, not a procedural requirement for participation.
